# Agent-bound tokens + mTLS

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P2 · Proven identity](../README.md#phase-2--proven-identity) · **Lane:** Worker · **Label:** `feature:identity-enforcement` · **Epic:** [#110](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/110) · **Tickets:** 10 (5S 5M)

Workers verify CP-issued Warden tokens using keys from the verified signed bundle, check that each token was minted for the agent the worker serves and for a key that is still registered, and can run an agent in `require` mode, where traffic without a valid bound token is refused. Workers call the CP over mTLS with the renewing worker cert instead of a bearer token. Everything is default-off and builds on the P1 internal/identity package, so off and attribute deployments behave exactly as in P1.

## How we build it

- Scope: require mode and agent binding on the worker, built on the P1 internal/identity package (W-P1-VRFY-01/02/07) and the verified bundle from W-P2-SBND-04. Nothing in this feature exists in the code yet; internal/identity, the identityP holder and RecordIdentityVerify come from P1, and the bundle, registry and token service come from P2.
- Per-worker agent binding: one worker serves one agent. The worker's agent id is the one W-P2-AREG-05 resolves (`warden run --agent-id`, then `central.agentID`, then worker.defaultAgentID, validated with agentid.ValidID), so judge lookups, the MCP session key, the decision line agent_id and binding use one value; this feature adds no key or flag of its own. A port-derived `agent:<port>` id is never registered, so binding fails with agent_unregistered. Several agents sharing one worker cannot be told apart in P2, and the docs say so.
- Mode resolution for the bound agent stays in settings, as in W-P1-VRFY-07 and p2-agent-registry: SettingsWire agents[].identity for the bound id, then identity.defaultMode, then off. W-P2-WBND-03 lets the CP serve `require` there; a standalone (local-only) worker has no signed bundle, so its local YAML keeps rejecting require. A P1 worker that receives require keeps its previous identity config (W-P1-VRFY-07), which is the rollout risk W-P2-WBND-07 guards. The worker logs the effective mode and its source at startup and on change.
- Rollout safety: under W-P1-VRFY-07 an old worker ignores a mode it does not know and would stay in attribute mode. Workers that implement require mode add `identity/require-v1` to the heartbeat caps (next to blocklist/v1 and agentreg/v1); the bound agentID is already reported by W-P2-AREG-05. The CP refuses a settings save that sets require for an agent (409 workers_lack_capability, overridable with an audited admin-only force) while a connected worker bound to that agent lacks the cap, and agents[].identity and identity.defaultMode become admin-only fields.
- Bundle inputs: the worker takes token keys from the bundle `sections.tokenJWKS` (W-P2-SBND-02), the issuer from the top-level bundle field `tokenIssuer` (added by W-P2-WBND-06), and agent status and key thumbprints from `registeredAgents[].{status,jkt}` (W-P2-AREG-04). Warden tokens carry `email` and `email_verified` (only when verified) and the JOSE header typ `wt+jwt` (W-P2-TOKX-02). The worker takes all of these only from `RemoteProvider.Bundle()`, which reports only bundles that passed bundle.Verify against pinned keys (W-P2-SBND-04); a worker without pins gets no keys, and the worker never fetches keys from the CP at runtime.
- Warden token verifier (new internal/identity/warden.go, next to the P1 OIDC verifier): alg is EdDSA or ES256 and must match the JWK kty and crv; typ is wt+jwt; kid must be in the bundle JWKS; iss equals tokenIssuer byte for byte; aud contains `warden-worker`, which is deliberately distinct from the P1 Dex data-plane audience `warden` (W-P1-DEX-01), so the two token kinds cannot be confused; exp and nbf use identity.clockSkewSeconds (default 60s, max 5m); exp-iat is at most 15m (ttl_too_long); sub, act.sub, sid, jti and cnf.jkt are required (missing_claim); tokens over 16 KiB are rejected before parsing.
- Dispatch and back-compat: a new identity.MultiVerifier reads the unverified iss after the size cap. tokenIssuer goes to the Warden verifier; identity.issuer goes to the P1 OIDC verifier only when `identity.acceptDexTokens` is true and is invalid with reason unbound_token when it is false; anything else is invalid with reason wrong_iss. acceptDexTokens is a *bool whose default is true when identity.issuer is set, so P1 attribute deployments keep status valid after upgrade. Dex tokens never satisfy require mode (reason unbound_token). Each accepted Dex token is counted with token_type=dex and produces at most one deprecation WARN per hour. The worker refuses to install a bundle keyset whose tokenIssuer equals identity.issuer.
- Claims and subject: identity.Claims gains Act, CnfJKT, Scope, KID and TokenType (dex|warden). identity.SubjectFrom fills the existing Subject{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, AgentID=act.sub}; no new principal type is added, so policy, block-list and MCP code keep one subject type. Group normalization and caps are the same as P1. Scope is parsed but not enforced or stored in P2.
- Binding, checked on every use and never cached: the bound agent must be in the bundle (agent_unregistered) with status active (agent_disabled); act.sub must equal the bound agent id (agent_mismatch); cnf.jkt must be in that agent's `jkt` list (cnf_mismatch). This gives agent match plus key liveness: removing a key or disabling an agent invalidates outstanding tokens within one long-poll. It is not proof of possession, because the token is a bearer token, and the docs say so. A signed per-CONNECT proof or agent client certs (cnf x5t#S256) are a later follow-up outside P2. The worker does not see allowed_groups, so a token minted before an agent's allowed_groups shrank stays valid until exp (at most tokenService.ttl, 15m); this is an accepted P2 gap, and disabling the agent or blocking the user cuts it at once.
- Snapshot and hot path: {generation, tokenIssuer, jwks, agents (id to status and jkt set)} is built once per verified bundle apply and swapped atomically. The P1 result LRU is keyed by (generation, sha256(token)), so an emergency key removal (W-P2-KEYS-05) takes effect on the next request. Cost per CONNECT: one cached lookup, or one EdDSA/ES256 verify when uncached, plus a few map lookups; budgets are the P1 ones (p99 under 100µs cached, under 1ms uncached, no network I/O).
- Require-mode enforcement: after the W-P2-AREG-05 agent_disabled check (403), the CONNECT must carry a valid, bound Warden token in Proxy-Authorization (Basic session:<token> or Bearer). Otherwise the worker returns 407 with `Proxy-Authenticate: Basic realm="warden"` and JSON {"error":"identity_required","reason":"<reason>"} before the block-list check, policy evaluation or any dial, and stores a deny event. On terminated traffic (HTTP/1, h2 streams, WebSocket upgrade, MCP over HTTP) identity failures are 403 JSON with Connection: close where applicable and never 401 or WWW-Authenticate, because a 401 after TLS termination looks like an upstream challenge and starts credential or OAuth discovery in MCP clients. An X-Warden-Identity header with a different sub or act gets 403 identity_conflict. MCP denies stay plain JSON like the existing mcpRequestScan 403; there is no JSON-RPC error body. The block list (W-P1-BLOCK-02) and default-deny policy, including GPOL EvaluateFor with the Warden subject, still run after identity passes. Before the first verified bundle, all require-mode traffic is denied.
- Token expiry on open connections: the CONNECT identity is valid until exp plus skew. A request after that gets 403 identity_expired with Connection: close; idle HTTP/1 keep-alives are closed at exp; h2 connections get GOAWAY and in-flight streams finish within existing timeouts; raw tunnels and WebSockets close at exp plus skew. This runs through the W-P1-BLOCK-05 session registry with an expiry timer, so clients and `warden identity exec` reconnect with a fresh token.
- Recording: analytics.Event gains UserAct (json user_act) and IdentityTokenType (json identity_token_type), both omitempty, so unattributed events and receipts stay byte-identical. The worker SQLite store adds columns; the CP fleet store columns are a separate CP ticket. The warden.decision.v1 schema gets user_act and token_type with a schema_rev bump. Tokens, cnf values and Authorization headers are never logged, stored or put in error bodies.
- Metrics: extend the P1 instrument warden.identity.verify.total{result,reason} with a bounded token_type label (dex|warden|none) and the reasons agent_mismatch, cnf_mismatch, agent_disabled, agent_unregistered, unbound_token and missing_claim; P1 reasons such as wrong_iss, unknown_kid, alg_not_allowed, ttl_too_long and jwks_unavailable are reused. There is no agent or sub label. Require-mode denials count on the existing warden.blocked.total with reasons identity_required, identity_expired and identity_conflict. A gauge warden.controlplane.clock_skew_seconds is estimated from the CP Date header on each long-poll. The worker dashboard identity summary is computed from stored events, because internal/dashboard does not read OTel metrics.
- Worker-to-CP mTLS comes from p2-worker-ca: W-P2-WCA-03 builds the one cert-presenting client (`controlPlane.enrollment`, or `controlPlane.clientCert`/`clientKey` for an external PKI) used by RemoteProvider and HTTPRemoteStore and sends no Authorization header once a cert is loaded. W-P2-WBND-05 adds no config; it proves the no-downgrade and mid-poll renewal behaviour this feature relies on. In P2 only /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest are called this way; P3 adds POST /control/user-token (W-P3-PUS-07) and POST /control/connect/pending (W-P3-JIT-01) on the same client, both cert-only (mTLS), rate-limited, with the CP re-verifying the user token on each call; /central/secrets stays a human-only route. A worker-aggregator central target keeps its bearer token.
- Degraded modes: with the CP down, workers keep verifying with keys from the last-known-good bundle in memory; no new tokens can be minted, so require-mode agents fail closed at most one token TTL (15 minutes) later. Operators alert on a rise in warden.identity.verify.total{result="expired"}. With Dex down, exchange fails at the CP and existing Warden tokens work until exp; the worker never contacts Dex for Warden tokens. A restart with the CP down reloads the bundle only from the opt-in W-P2-SBND-06 cache (`<controlPlane.stateDir>/bundle/`); without it the worker stays fail-closed. A client cert that expires during a CP outage keeps the last-known-good policy (W-P2-WCA-03).
- Carry-forward from p1-block-list: no agent-kind block entry is added. Require mode closes the token-less gap that W-P1-BLOCK-02 left, and registry status=disabled, enforced by the worker as agent_disabled, is the agent-level kill switch.

## Done when

On a compose deployment with a CP (token service, signed bundles, worker CA, agent registry) and one enrolled worker bound with `--agent-id` (W-P2-AREG-05) to a registered agent whose settings entry is in require mode, where the CP refused the switch while a worker without identity/require-v1 was connected: CONNECTs with no token, a Dex ID token, an expired, forged or unknown-kid Warden token, a token minted for another agent, a token whose agent key was removed, or a token for a disabled agent each get 407, no upstream dial and a deny event with the matching reason. A Warden token from POST /oauth2/token for a permitted user is accepted, and its local event, decision line and fleet event carry sub, act, sid, groups and token_type=warden with no token in any log. Blocking that user by email, or disabling the agent, denies new requests and closes open sessions within one long-poll cycle. Open connections close at token exp and the identity exec forwarder reconnects with a fresh token. With the CP stopped the worker keeps accepting unexpired tokens from its last-known-good bundle and denies everything after they expire, and a worker started before its first verified bundle denies all traffic. An attribute-mode agent on a P1 config still records Dex tokens as valid. All worker calls to /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest use the renewing client cert with no Authorization header, and a renewal mid-run does not drop the long-poll.

### 1/10 · W-P2-WBND-01

**Verify CP-issued Warden tokens against verified bundle keys**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#111](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/111)

Add a Warden token verifier to the P1 internal/identity package that takes its keys, issuer and agents only from the last signed bundle that passed bundle.Verify, swapped atomically on each bundle apply. A dispatcher routes tokens by issuer so P1 Dex tokens keep working in attribute mode, and the result uses the existing identity.Claims and identity.Subject types. Nothing changes until a CP serves a bundle with tokenIssuer and jwks.

**Requirements**

- New internal/identity/warden.go: WardenVerifier implementing the P1 identity.Verifier interface. Allowed algs are exactly EdDSA and ES256, and the header alg must match the JWK kty/crv (none, HS* and RS* give alg_not_allowed). Header typ must be `wt+jwt` (else malformed). kid must be in the bundle `sections.tokenJWKS` (else unknown_kid). iss must equal the bundle `tokenIssuer` byte for byte. aud must contain the new constant identity.WardenWorkerAudience = "warden-worker", which is deliberately distinct from the P1 Dex data-plane audience `warden` (W-P1-DEX-01).
- exp and nbf are checked with the P1 identity.clockSkewSeconds setting (default 60s, max 5m); exp-iat above 15m gives ttl_too_long; missing sub, act.sub, sid, jti or cnf.jkt gives the new reason missing_claim; tokens over 16 KiB give too_large before parsing. Signatures are checked with internal/keys.Verify (W-P2-KEYS-01).
- identity.Claims gains Act, CnfJKT, Scope, KID and TokenType (dex|warden). SubjectFrom sets Subject.AgentID from act.sub and fills Email and EmailVerified from the token's email and email_verified claims. No Principal type is added. Scope is parsed but not enforced or stored.
- New identity.MultiVerifier reads the unverified iss after the size cap: tokenIssuer goes to the WardenVerifier, identity.issuer goes to the P1 OIDC verifier only when acceptDexTokens resolves true and gives invalid/unbound_token when it resolves false, and any other iss gives invalid/wrong_iss. A Dex token never satisfies require mode (reason unbound_token, applied in W-P2-WBND-03).
- New config field identity.acceptDexTokens (*bool, json/yaml acceptDexTokens, omitempty) on IdentitySettings and the local identity block, with DeepCopy and SettingsWire round-trip support. Unset resolves to true when identity.issuer is set and false otherwise. Each valid Dex token is recorded with token_type=dex and logs at most one WARN per hour naming the deprecation, with no token data.
- Keys come only from `RemoteProvider.Bundle()` (W-P2-SBND-04), which reports only bundles verified against pinned keys; a worker without pins (legacy wire) installs no keys. Before the first verified bundle, Warden tokens return unverified/jwks_unavailable. A tokenIssuer equal to identity.issuer is refused with one ERROR log and leaves keys unavailable. The worker never fetches keys from the CP at runtime.
- The snapshot {generation, tokenIssuer, jwks, agents} is swapped atomically with a monotonically increasing generation, and the P1 result LRU is keyed by (generation, sha256(token)), so a kid removed from the bundle stops verifying on the next request.
- Raw tokens never appear in logs, errors, events or test output; debug logs carry only kid and an 8-hex sha256 fingerprint. The cached path stays under 100µs p99 and an uncached verify under 1ms, recorded under warden.request.added_latency stage=identity.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/identity (from W-P1-VRFY-01): extend Claims with Act, CnfJKT, Scope, KID and TokenType; extend SubjectFrom; add reasons missing_claim and unbound_token to the bounded Reason set and add them to docs/identity-contract.md so TestContractDocMatchesConstants stays green.
2. New internal/identity/warden.go: WardenVerifier with an atomic.Pointer to a new keySnapshot type and SetBundle(tokenIssuer string, jwks []keys.JWK, generation int64); verification as in the requirements using internal/keys.Verify.
3. New internal/identity/multi.go: MultiVerifier dispatch by unverified iss, deprecation WARN rate limiter for Dex tokens, cache key including the generation.
4. internal/config: add IdentitySettings.AcceptDexTokens *bool plus a resolver method, local YAML field, DeepCopy and validation.
5. internal/worker/applier.go: in SettingsApplier.Apply, after the long-poll applies a verified bundle (W-P2-SBND-04), call WardenVerifier.SetBundle and swap the MultiVerifier through the P1 identityP holder (W-P1-VRFY-07). internal/worker/worker.go does the same at startup when the W-P2-SBND-06 cache was loaded.
6. Tests: internal/identity TestWardenVerifier, TestWardenKeysetSwap (-race), TestMultiVerifierDispatch and BenchmarkWardenVerify; internal/config TestIdentityAcceptDexTokensDefault; internal/worker TestBundleAppliesTokenKeys with a fake CP.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a bundle JWKS with EdDSA kid K1: a valid K1 token returns valid with TokenType=warden and Subject.AgentID=act.sub; a K2-signed token gives unknown_kid; alg none and HS256 signed with the public key give alg_not_allowed; aud `warden` gives wrong_aud; exp-iat=20m gives ttl_too_long; missing cnf gives missing_claim. Command: `go test ./internal/identity -run TestWardenVerifier`.
- [ ] A token cached as valid under K1 returns unknown_kid on the next Verify after a bundle without K1 is applied, and K2 tokens from the new bundle verify without a restart, with 100 concurrent verifications during the swap: `go test -race ./internal/identity -run TestWardenKeysetSwap`.
- [ ] With identity.issuer set and acceptDexTokens absent, a valid Dex token returns valid with TokenType=dex; with acceptDexTokens false it returns invalid/unbound_token; with no identity.issuer the default resolves to false: `go test ./internal/config ./internal/identity -run 'TestIdentityAcceptDexTokensDefault|TestMultiVerifierDispatch'`.
- [ ] A fake CP serving bundle v1 and then v2 with a rotated key causes a keyset swap with zero requests to any JWKS endpoint, and a worker with no pins (legacy wire) leaves Warden tokens at unverified/jwks_unavailable: `go test ./internal/worker -run TestBundleAppliesTokenKeys`.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identity -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkWardenVerify -benchmem` shows the cached path under 100µs/op, and a captured slog buffer from the tests above contains no substring of any test token.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-VRFY-07`](identity-verification.md#77--w-p1-vrfy-07) Wire the identity verifier into worker assembly, hot reload and deployment; [`W-P2-SBND-04`](signed-bundles.md#47--w-p2-sbnd-04) Verify signed bundles in RemoteProvider and keep last-known-good in memory; [`W-P2-KEYS-01`](key-management.md#17--w-p2-keys-01) Add internal/keys Signer, JWK and RFC 7638 kid helpers; [`W-P2-WBND-04`](identity-enforcement.md#410--w-p2-wbnd-04) Extend identity metrics with token type and binding reasons; [`W-P2-WBND-06`](identity-enforcement.md#610--w-p2-wbnd-06) Add token issuer, agent key thumbprints and email claims to CP outputs

**Unblocks:** [`W-P2-WBND-02`](identity-enforcement.md#210--w-p2-wbnd-02) Bind Warden tokens to the worker's registered agent and key; [`W-P3-PUS-07`](refresh-model.md#712--w-p3-pus-07) Add the worker-mTLS mint endpoint POST /control/user-token

### 2/10 · W-P2-WBND-02

**Bind Warden tokens to the worker's registered agent and key**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#112](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/112)

Using the worker agent id from W-P2-AREG-05, check that every Warden token was minted for that agent, that the agent is active, and that the token's cnf.jkt is one of the agent's current registry keys. This gives agent match plus key liveness, not proof of possession, and the docs say so. Record the agent (act) on worker events and decision lines.

**Requirements**

- The bound agent id is the one W-P2-AREG-05 resolves (`--agent-id`, then `central.agentID`, then worker.defaultAgentID); this ticket adds no config key or flag, so existing judge lookups do not change.
- Binding runs in the P1 proxy identity resolvers (W-P1-VRFY-02) after signature verification, for Warden tokens only, in this order: bound agent not in the bundle agents gives agent_unregistered; status disabled gives agent_disabled; act.sub different from the bound agent gives agent_mismatch; cnf.jkt not in that agent's `jkt` list from Policy.RegisteredAgents (W-P2-AREG-04) gives cnf_mismatch. Every failure gives status invalid and a nil Subject.
- Binding is checked on every use against the current snapshot and never cached. The thumbprint lookup is a map[string]struct{} built on bundle apply in the same atomic snapshot as the keyset, with 0 allocs/op.
- In attribute mode a binding failure is recorded and the request continues as anonymous per policy. The block-list check (W-P1-BLOCK-02) still matches the parsed sub and email, because a match can only deny.
- analytics.Event gains UserAct (json user_act) and IdentityTokenType (json identity_token_type), both omitempty, stamped only for valid identities, with local SQLite columns through addColumnIfAbsent in insertColumns, StoreEvent, StoreEventsBatch, GetEvents and GetOldestEventIDs. Identity-free events stay byte-identical.
- decisionLog and the warden.decision.v1 schema gain user_act and token_type with a schema_rev bump. Tokens and cnf values are never logged.
- docs/identity-contract.md and docs/control-plane.md state the guarantee (agent match and key liveness within one long-poll, not proof of possession), the one-agent-per-worker rule, and that a port-derived id such as `agent:8080` never matches a registry id.

**Implementation plan**

1. Reuse the W-P2-AREG-05 resolved agent id from the worker options; add no config key or flag.
2. internal/worker/worker.go: pass the resolved id into the identity binding check and log it with the effective mode and its source at startup.
3. internal/identity: new BindingCheck(snapshot, agentID, claims) (Reason, ok) next to WardenVerifier, reading the agents map from the W-P2-WBND-01 snapshot; add reasons agent_mismatch, cnf_mismatch, agent_disabled and agent_unregistered to the Reason set and the contract doc.
4. internal/proxy identity resolvers (resolveConnIdentity and resolveRequestIdentity from W-P1-VRFY-02): call BindingCheck after a valid Warden verify and downgrade the status on failure.
5. internal/analytics/analytics.go and the SQLite store: add UserAct and IdentityTokenType with migrations; internal/proxy recordEvent (W-P1-VRFY-03) stamps them; extend decisionLog and the decision schema file.
6. Tests: internal/proxy TestIdentityBinding subtests and BenchmarkBindingCheck; internal/worker TestBindingKeyRemovalAppliesOnLongPoll; internal/analytics TestMigrateUserActColumn.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With bundle agents A (thumbprint T1) and B and a worker bound to B, a valid token with act.sub=A on CONNECT gives invalid/agent_mismatch and a nil Subject: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityBinding/agent_mismatch`.
- [ ] With the worker bound to A, a token with cnf.jkt=T9 gives cnf_mismatch, a token for a disabled A gives agent_disabled, and a worker bound to `agent:8080` gives agent_unregistered: `go test ./internal/proxy -run 'TestIdentityBinding/(cnf_mismatch|agent_disabled|agent_unregistered)'`.

### 3/10 · W-P2-WBND-03

**Enforce identity require mode on CONNECT and terminated traffic**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#113](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/113)

Add the `require` mode for an agent whose served settings entry (agents[].identity) asks for it. A CONNECT without a valid, bound Warden token gets 407 before any dial, and identity failures inside a terminated tunnel get 403 JSON. The worker fails closed before its first verified bundle and advertises the identity/require-v1 heartbeat cap so the CP can refuse require for agents served by old workers.

**Requirements**

- Mode resolution for the bound agent: SettingsWire agents[].identity for the W-P2-AREG-05 agent id, then identity.defaultMode, then off. config validation now accepts `require` in served SettingsWire (CP write path and parseRemotePolicy); local YAML on a worker without controlPlane.endpoint keeps rejecting it, so a standalone worker never enters require. The effective mode and its source are logged on change and shown on /dashboard/api/status.
- CONNECT in require mode: the W-P2-AREG-05 agent_disabled check runs first (403). Proxy-Authorization is mandatory and must verify (W-P2-WBND-01) and bind (W-P2-WBND-02) with TokenType=warden. Otherwise the worker writes 407 Proxy Authentication Required with `Proxy-Authenticate: Basic realm="warden"`, Content-Type application/json, Connection: close and body {"error":"identity_required","reason":"<bounded reason>"}, before the block-list check, Policy.Evaluate and any dial, and stores a deny event with the new Reason identity_required in internal/proxy/reasons.go.
- Terminated traffic (runRequestStages, serveGRPCStream, WebSocket upgrade in ws.go, MCP over HTTP): an X-Warden-Identity header whose sub or act differs from the CONNECT identity gets 403 identity_conflict; a request after the CONNECT identity's exp plus skew gets 403 identity_expired with Connection: close; h2 streams get 403 on the stream. No 401 or WWW-Authenticate is ever written, and MCP denies are plain JSON like the existing mcpRequestScan 403, with no JSON-RPC body.
- Fail closed: in require mode, before the first verified bundle, with an empty keyset, or with an unregistered bound agent, every CONNECT gets 407 with reason jwks_unavailable or agent_unregistered. A bundle loaded from the opt-in W-P2-SBND-06 cache lifts this at restart without the CP.
- Default-deny is unchanged: the block list (W-P1-BLOCK-02) and policy evaluation, including GPOL EvaluateFor with the Warden subject, still run after identity passes. Attribute and off modes are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- RemoteProvider.Heartbeat adds `identity/require-v1` to caps; the bound agentID is already sent by W-P2-AREG-05. Old CPs ignore the cap.
- Denials increment warden.blocked.total with reasons identity_required, identity_expired and identity_conflict, and warden.requests.total{decision="deny"}. Response bodies carry only bounded reason codes. The new mode, error codes and reasons are added to docs/identity-contract.md so TestContractDocMatchesConstants passes.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/identity: add ModeRequire; internal/config: new EffectiveIdentityMode(agentID, agents []AgentIdentity, settings) resolver returning mode and source; accept require in served SettingsWire and keep rejecting it in the local YAML of a standalone worker.
2. internal/worker/applier.go and worker.go: compute the effective mode on each apply and pass it to proxy SetIdentity; log mode and source; expose them in the /dashboard/api/status payload.
3. internal/proxy/serve.go handleConn: in require mode, after identity resolution and before the block-list check, write the 407 through a new denyIdentityRequired helper and store the deny event via recordEvent.
4. internal/proxy/http.go identityStage, grpc.go serveGRPCStream and ws.go upgrade path: new writeIdentityDenied(w, code, reason) helper for 403 identity_required, identity_expired and identity_conflict.
5. internal/config/remote.go Heartbeat: add caps entry identity/require-v1.
6. Tests: internal/proxy TestIdentityRequireMode subtests (connect_no_token, connect_dex_token, conflict, expired_http, h2_stream, ws_upgrade, mcp_http); internal/worker TestRequireModeBeforeFirstBundle; internal/config TestEffectiveIdentityMode and TestRequireRejectedInStandaloneYAML; internal/proxy TestIdentityAttributeModeUnchanged.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] In require mode with a bundle applied, a CONNECT with no Proxy-Authorization gets 407 with `Proxy-Authenticate: Basic realm="warden"` and an identity_required body, the fake dialer records zero dials, and one deny event has Reason=identity_required: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityRequireMode/connect_no_token`.
- [ ] In require mode with no bundle yet, CONNECTs with no token, a Dex token and a forged Warden token all get 407 and zero dials occur: `go test ./internal/worker -run TestRequireModeBeforeFirstBundle`.
- [ ] With TLS termination and a valid CONNECT token, a request after exp plus skew gets 403 identity_expired, a different-sub X-Warden-Identity gets 403 identity_conflict, an h2 stream gets 403 on the stream, and no response carries 401 or WWW-Authenticate: `go test ./internal/proxy -run 'TestIdentityRequireMode/(expired_http|conflict|h2_stream|mcp_http)'`.
- [ ] In attribute mode an invalid token is still forwarded when policy allows, with identity_status invalid: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityAttributeModeUnchanged`.
- [ ] A served SettingsWire with agents[].identity=require applies require to the bound agent, a standalone worker's local YAML with require is rejected, and the heartbeat body contains identity/require-v1: `go test ./internal/config -run 'TestEffectiveIdentityMode|TestRequireRejectedInStandaloneYAML|TestHeartbeatCaps'`.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identity -run TestContractDocMatchesConstants` passes with the new mode and reasons documented.

**Depends on:** [`W-P2-WBND-02`](identity-enforcement.md#210--w-p2-wbnd-02) Bind Warden tokens to the worker's registered agent and key; [`W-P1-BLOCK-02`](user-block-list.md#29--w-p1-block-02) Enforce the block list in the worker at CONNECT, per request and per h2 stream; [`W-P1-IDC-01`](identity-contract.md#14--w-p1-idc-01) Write the agent identity contract for harness builders; [`W-P2-AREG-05`](agent-registry.md#57--w-p2-areg-05) Bind workers to an agent id and enforce agent_disabled

### 4/10 · W-P2-WBND-04

**Extend identity metrics with token type and binding reasons**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#114](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/114)

Extend the P1 instrument warden.identity.verify.total instead of adding new failure counters, so the verifier and binding tickets record through it from their first PR. Add a bounded token_type label, the new binding reasons, a CP clock-skew gauge and an identity summary in the worker dashboard built from stored events.

**Requirements**

- RecordIdentityVerify (W-P1-VRFY-02) gains a token_type argument with values dex|warden|none and accepts the new reasons agent_mismatch, cnf_mismatch, agent_disabled, agent_unregistered, unbound_token and missing_claim. No new identity counter and no warden_identity_failures_total or warden_identity_verified_total.
- Reason and token_type are fixed Go constants; any unknown value is recorded as `other`, so cardinality stays bounded. Labels never carry sub, email, sid, jti, kid, agent id or token material.
- RecordBlocked accepts identity_required, identity_expired and identity_conflict, used by W-P2-WBND-03 and W-P2-WBND-09.
- New gauge warden.controlplane.clock_skew_seconds (no labels), set from the CP Date header on each RemoteProvider.PollLong response, to diagnose mass expired or nbf failures.
- The worker dashboard analytics response (/dashboard/api/analytics) gains an `identity` block computed from stored events: counts by identity_status and the top 5 identity_reason values in the range. The block is omitted when no event has identity fields.
- docs/control-plane.md lists the label values and recommends alerts on the non-valid share, on token_type=dex for deprecation tracking, and on result=expired during CP outages.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/observability/observability.go: extend RecordIdentityVerify(result, reason, tokenType) with allowlist normalisation; keep it nil-safe; update the P1 callers in internal/proxy to pass token_type.
2. internal/observability: register the clock-skew gauge; internal/config/remote.go PollLong reports the Date-header delta through a new optional callback set by internal/worker.
3. internal/dashboard: add the identity block to the analytics handler, reading identity_status and identity_reason from the event store.
4. docs/control-plane.md: metric and alert section.
5. Tests: internal/observability TestRecordIdentityVerifyTokenType and TestRecordIdentityVerifyBounded with the OTel manual reader; internal/dashboard TestIdentitySummary; internal/config TestPollLongClockSkew.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With a manual OTel reader, each new reason increments exactly one series with the expected result and token_type, and a valid Dex token increments {result=valid,token_type=dex}: `go test ./internal/observability -run TestRecordIdentityVerifyTokenType`.
- [ ] An unknown reason or token_type is recorded as `other`, and nil Metrics does not panic: `go test ./internal/observability -run TestRecordIdentityVerifyBounded`.
- [ ] Given stored events with statuses valid, invalid/cnf_mismatch and none, GET /dashboard/api/analytics returns an identity block with those counts, and with no identity events the block is absent: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestIdentitySummary`.
- [ ] A fake CP whose Date header is 120s ahead sets warden.controlplane.clock_skew_seconds to about 120: `go test ./internal/config -run TestPollLongClockSkew`.

### 5/10 · W-P2-WBND-05

**Use the worker mTLS client cert for all CP calls**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#115](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/115)

W-P2-WCA-03 already builds the one cert-presenting CP client (`controlPlane.enrollment`, or `controlPlane.clientCert`/`clientKey`) for RemoteProvider and HTTPRemoteStore, so this ticket adds no config keys or transport. It proves the properties require mode depends on: every worker-plane CP call presents the cert, no call ever falls back to a bearer token, and a renewal never drops the long-poll. If p2-worker-bound adds a new CP call, it must use the same client.

**Requirements**

- No new config: `controlPlane.auth`, `central.auth`, `clientCertFile` and `clientKeyFile` are not added; the W-P2-WCA-03 keys are the only switches.
- Pull, PollLong, Heartbeat, HTTPRemoteStore SendBatch and SendMCP all go through the W-P2-WCA-03 client and send no Authorization header once a cert is loaded, also after the CP returns 401 and after the cert expires.
- A renewal swap during a held long-poll does not cancel it; the next handshake presents the new serial (W-P2-WCA-03 CloseIdleConnections).
- A worker-aggregator central target that is not the CP keeps its bearer token.
- Key material and PEM never reach logs; the existing `warden_worker_cert_expiry_seconds` gauge from W-P2-WCA-03 is the only expiry metric.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/worker: add TestControlPlaneMTLSClient and TestControlPlaneCertRenewMidPoll against an httptest TLS CP that requires a client cert and rejects any Authorization header.
2. internal/config and internal/analytics: add TestRemoteProviderNoBearerWithCert and TestHTTPRemoteStoreNoBearerWithCert covering the 401 and expired-cert cases.
3. Fix any CP call path the tests find that bypasses the W-P2-WCA-03 client.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Against an httptest TLS CP that requires a client cert and rejects any Authorization header, Pull, PollLong, Heartbeat, SendBatch and SendMCP all succeed: `go test ./internal/worker -run TestControlPlaneMTLSClient`.
- [ ] When the holder swaps to a renewed cert during a held long-poll, the poll completes with 200 and the next handshake presents the new serial: `go test -race ./internal/worker -run TestControlPlaneCertRenewMidPoll`.
- [ ] With a cert loaded and tokenEnv also set, no request seen by the fake CP carries Authorization, including after it starts returning 401: `go test ./internal/config ./internal/analytics -run 'NoBearerWithCert'`.
- [ ] With no enrollment and no clientCert configured, existing tests pass and the bearer header is still sent: `go test ./internal/config ./internal/analytics ./internal/worker`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P2-WCA-03`](worker-mtls.md#38--w-p2-wca-03) Add worker enrollment, auto-renew and cert-based CP client

**Unblocks:** [`W-P2-WBND-10`](identity-enforcement.md#1010--w-p2-wbnd-10) Test require mode and worker mTLS end to end

### 6/10 · W-P2-WBND-06

**Add token issuer, agent key thumbprints and email claims to CP outputs**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#267](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/267)

CP half of agent binding. Key thumbprints already reach workers as `registeredAgents[].jkt` (W-P2-AREG-04), and minted tokens already carry email, email_verified and typ wt+jwt (W-P2-TOKX-02). This ticket adds the one missing input, the token issuer inside the signed bundle, plus the issuer collision check, and checks the other two contracts end to end.

**Requirements**

- The signed Bundle (internal/bundle, W-P2-SBND-01/02) gains a top-level `tokenIssuer` (omitempty), set from tokenService.issuer and included in the signed payload and in contentSha256.
- CP config validation rejects tokenService.issuer equal to identity.issuer, naming both keys.
- Check only, no new field: `registeredAgents[].jkt` uses the same keys.Thumbprint value as cnf.jkt in minted tokens, and a registry key change refreshes the bundle through the W-P2-AREG-04 publish_log path.
- Check only: tokens minted by W-P2-TOKX-02 carry email and email_verified only for a verified email, and header typ `wt+jwt`.
- The new field is omitempty, so bundles without it still parse in W-P2-SBND-04 and old workers ignore it. No key material other than public thumbprints and the issuer string enters the bundle, logs or audit entries.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/bundle: add TokenIssuer to Bundle and to the contentSha256 helper; extend the bundle golden tests (no canonicalization: the payload bytes are signed as-is).
2. internal/controlplane policyserver buildBundle (W-P2-SBND-02): fill TokenIssuer from the tokenService config; add the issuer collision check to CP startup validation.
3. Tests: internal/bundle TestBundleTokenIssuerSigned; internal/controlplane TestBundleTokenIssuer, TestTokenIssuerCollisionRejected and TestBundleThumbprintMatchesCnf (registers a key, mints a token with W-P2-TOKX-02 and compares cnf.jkt with the served jkt).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A bundle served by the CP contains tokenIssuer inside the signed payload, and altering it fails bundle.Verify: `go test ./internal/bundle ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestBundleTokenIssuerSigned|TestBundleTokenIssuer'`.
- [ ] A token minted for a registered key has cnf.jkt equal to that agent's served `registeredAgents[].jkt`, and removing the key changes the served bundle on the next long-poll: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBundleThumbprintMatchesCnf`.
- [ ] CP config with tokenService.issuer equal to identity.issuer fails startup with an error naming both keys, and a bundle without tokenIssuer still verifies on the worker: `go test ./internal/controlplane ./internal/config -run 'TestTokenIssuerCollisionRejected|TestBundleWithoutTokenIssuer'`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P2-SBND-02`](signed-bundles.md#27--w-p2-sbnd-02) Serve the signed bundle envelope on GET /policy behind --bundles; [`W-P2-AREG-04`](agent-registry.md#47--w-p2-areg-04) Serve registered agents in the policy wire; [`W-P2-TOKX-02`](token-exchange.md#27--w-p2-tokx-02) Implement token exchange policy checks and JWT minting; [`W-P2-TOKX-03`](token-exchange.md#37--w-p2-tokx-03) Mount POST /oauth2/token with RFC 8693 request parsing and config

### 7/10 · W-P2-WBND-07

**Refuse require mode for agents served by workers without the capability**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#268](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/268)

CP rollout guard for require mode. An old worker keeps attribute mode when it receives a mode it does not know (W-P1-VRFY-07), so switching an agent to require while such a worker serves it would fail open. The CP refuses that switch unless an admin forces it, and the console flags such workers.

**Requirements**

- Use the agentID and caps that W-P2-AREG-03 and W-P1-BLOCK-04 already store per worker; no new heartbeat field.
- A settings save (POST/PUT /dashboard/api/settings, and a held draft when it is applied under p2-approvals) that sets agents[].identity=require for an agent id, or identity.defaultMode=require, returns 409 {"error":"workers_lack_capability","workers":[ids]} when any connected worker reporting that agentID (or any connected worker, for defaultMode) lacks identity/require-v1.
- A `force=true` query parameter overrides the check; only admins may force, and the admin audit entry records force and the listed worker ids.
- agents[].identity and identity.defaultMode become admin-only fields in the W-P1-SSO-05 per-field settings check, so an editor cannot downgrade an agent from require.
- The Agents page (W-P2-AREG-03) and the worker list show 'N connected workers for this agent do not enforce require mode' when such workers exist.
- Workers that send no agentID are listed as 'agent unknown' and do not block a per-agent switch; docs/control-plane.md tells operators to set `--agent-id` or central.agentID on every worker before using require.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/controlplane settings write path (WriteSettings): capability check before persisting a require mode, force override and audit fields.
2. internal/controlplane authz per-field table (W-P1-SSO-05): mark agents[].identity and identity.defaultMode admin-only.
3. internal/dashboard index.html and handlers: warning on the Agents page and the worker list.
4. docs/control-plane.md: runbook for moving an agent from attribute to require, with the capability check and rollback.
5. Tests: internal/controlplane TestRequireRefusedForOldWorkers, TestRequireForceAudited and TestIdentityModeAdminOnly.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With a connected worker reporting agentID=a1 and caps [blocklist/v1, agentreg/v1], a settings save that sets agents[a1].identity=require returns 409 workers_lack_capability listing that worker: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestRequireRefusedForOldWorkers`.
- [ ] The same save with force=true by an admin succeeds and writes an audit entry with force and the worker ids: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestRequireForceAudited`.
- [ ] An editor changing agents[].identity or identity.defaultMode gets 403 role_required, and after the worker heartbeats with identity/require-v1 an admin save succeeds without force: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestIdentityModeAdminOnly`.

### 9/10 · W-P2-WBND-09

**Close require-mode sessions at token expiry and document require mode**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#270](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/270)

A CONNECT-bound Warden token lasts 15 minutes, but raw tunnels, keep-alives, h2 connections and WebSockets can stay open far longer. Close require-mode sessions at token expiry through the W-P1-BLOCK-05 session registry, and close sessions whose agent or key was revoked by a bundle change. Write the require-mode section of the identity contract.

**Requirements**

- Sessions in require mode register in the W-P1-BLOCK-05 session registry with their token exp and kid. A single expiry timer (a min-heap, no per-connection goroutine) closes them: idle HTTP/1 keep-alives at exp; h2 connections get GOAWAY at exp and in-flight streams finish within existing timeouts; raw tunnels and WebSockets close at exp plus clockSkewSeconds.
- Each closure writes one deny event with Reason identity_expired and calls RecordBlocked("identity_expired").
- After each verified bundle apply, the registry re-checks require-mode sessions and closes those whose kid left the JWKS or whose binding now fails (agent disabled or key removed), with the matching reason.
- Attribute-mode and anonymous sessions are not registered for expiry, so they see no change.
- docs/identity-contract.md gains a require-mode section that adds to Contract v1 without changing any v1 header: Warden token on CONNECT, 407 and 403 bodies, the identity_conflict rule, close at exp, Dex tokens only in attribute mode, and that binding is agent match plus key liveness, not proof of possession.
- docs/control-plane.md documents degraded modes: CP down means require-mode agents fail closed one token TTL later; Dex down affects only new exchanges; a restart with the CP down reloads the bundle only from the opt-in W-P2-SBND-06 cache, otherwise it stays fail-closed.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/proxy session registry (W-P1-BLOCK-05): add exp and kid to the registered entry and a new expiry heap with one timer goroutine per Proxy.
2. internal/proxy tls.go, grpc.go, ws.go and the tunnel path: register require-mode sessions and implement the close behaviour per connection type (GOAWAY via the h2 server's graceful shutdown for that connection).
3. internal/proxy: new Proxy.RecheckIdentitySessions() called from the same post-apply hook as CloseBlockedSessions.
4. docs/identity-contract.md and docs/control-plane.md: require-mode and degraded-mode sections.
5. Tests: internal/proxy TestRequireSessionExpiry subtests (tunnel, keepalive, h2_goaway, websocket) with a fake clock, TestRecheckClosesRevokedKey, TestAttributeSessionsNotRegistered.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With a fake clock, an open raw tunnel closes within 1s of exp plus skew and writes one identity_expired deny event: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestRequireSessionExpiry/tunnel`.
- [ ] An h2 connection receives GOAWAY at exp while an in-flight stream completes, and an idle keep-alive is closed at exp: `go test ./internal/proxy -run 'TestRequireSessionExpiry/(h2_goaway|keepalive)'`.
- [ ] A bundle apply that removes the session's kid closes the session with reason unknown_kid: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestRecheckClosesRevokedKey`.
- [ ] Attribute-mode sessions are not registered and stay open past token exp: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestAttributeSessionsNotRegistered`.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identity -run TestContractDocMatchesConstants` passes with the require-mode section.

### 10/10 · W-P2-WBND-10

**Test require mode and worker mTLS end to end**

Type **test** · Size **M** · Issue [#271](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/271)

Prove the feature's done_when on a real CP and worker. An integration test mints a Warden token through POST /oauth2/token with an agent assertion, drives a require-mode worker bound to that agent, and checks every reject case, recording, revocation, expiry and mTLS-only CP access.

**Requirements**

- New test/integration/identity_require_test.go under the integration build tag in the existing test/integration package, with new helpers that start an in-process CP, token service, worker CA, agent registry and fake Dex.
- Covers 407 with zero dials for: no token, Dex token, expired, forged and unknown-kid Warden tokens, a token for another agent, a removed agent key and a disabled agent.
- Covers the accepted path: event, decision line and fleet event carry sub, act, sid, groups and token_type=warden, and no captured log contains the token.
- Covers block-by-email and agent disable closing open sessions within one long-poll, and session close at exp with reconnect using a fresh token.
- Covers degraded modes: CP stopped (unexpired tokens accepted, then denied after exp), restart before the first verified bundle (all denied), and an attribute-mode agent still recording Dex tokens as valid.
- Covers mTLS: the CP rejects any Authorization header on worker routes and the worker succeeds with its client cert, including across a forced renewal.

**Implementation plan**

1. test/integration: new helpers to start the CP with token service, worker CA and registry, enroll a worker and register an agent key.
2. New test/integration/identity_require_test.go with subtests for reject cases, accepted path, revocation, expiry, degraded modes and mTLS.
3. Drive expiry with tokenService.ttl set to its 1m minimum (W-P2-TOKX-03), so no test-only hook is needed.
4. Assert on stored events, decision log output and captured slog buffers.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test -tags=integration ./test/integration -run TestIdentityRequire` passes.
- [ ] Each reject subtest asserts a 407, zero upstream dials and the expected reason on warden.identity.verify.total.
- [ ] The mTLS subtest asserts that no request to /policy, /control/heartbeat or /central/ingest carried an Authorization header.
- [ ] No captured log line in the run contains any minted token.

**Depends on:** [`W-P2-WBND-03`](identity-enforcement.md#310--w-p2-wbnd-03) Enforce identity require mode on CONNECT and terminated traffic; [`W-P2-WBND-05`](identity-enforcement.md#510--w-p2-wbnd-05) Use the worker mTLS client cert for all CP calls; [`W-P2-WBND-06`](identity-enforcement.md#610--w-p2-wbnd-06) Add token issuer, agent key thumbprints and email claims to CP outputs; [`W-P2-WBND-07`](identity-enforcement.md#710--w-p2-wbnd-07) Refuse require mode for agents served by workers without the capability; [`W-P2-WBND-08`](identity-enforcement.md#810--w-p2-wbnd-08) Store agent and token type fields in the CP fleet store; [`W-P2-WBND-09`](identity-enforcement.md#910--w-p2-wbnd-09) Close require-mode sessions at token expiry and document require mode
